newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dead, wounded in fighting at key Afghan airbase.
newsitem.headline: Dead, wounded in fighting at key Afghan airbase.

text.p: Five people were killed and another 10 wounded in fighting around the Bagram military airfield north of Kabul on Wednesday, staff at the hospital at Charikar who treated them told reporters.

One of the wounded, 22-year-old Najibul Rachman, was still lying on the hospital operating table in his blood-soaked, clothing waiting for a doctor to perform surgery, six hours after being hit in both the legs and one wrist by fragments from a rocket-propelled grenade.
"My mother's house was burning and I went to try to put it out and the Taleban fired a grenade at me from their trenches about 15 metres (50 feet) away," the man told reporters.
"I was not the only one injured, there were a number of others who were wounded as well and I think some were killed."
The injured man described himself as a fighter for Ahmad Shah Masood, military chief of the government that was ousted by Taleban fighters a little more than two weeks ago.
Masood's men were driven from Kabul along with the rest of the government when forces of the purist Islamic militia swept into the capital.
Masood staged an orderly retreat to the Pansjher Valley and then regrouped before beginning to push back south towards Kabul.
A large swathe of territory north of the capital has changed hands several times in the past few weeks and civilians trapped in the fighting have had to use their wits to survive.
The airfield at Bagram and its surrounding villages have been fiercely contested for the past week.

Upon closer questioning the injured Rachman said he had worked as a military driver for Taleban when they occupied his hamlet and had then switched to Masood's forces when the Taleban were driven out.
The man had risked his life to try to keep his mother's house from burning. Now the house was destroyed and he was badly wounded, lying in an unspeakably filthy hospital without a surgeon.

The streets of Charikar outside were tumultuous under a stormy sky as refugees fled from points to the south where fighting was under way, and town residents joined them in anticipation of the battle moving north.
